record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: What observable cosmological consequences follow from using the Sorkin-Johnston state, a unique distinguished vacuum state that is well-defined for both causal sets and continuum curved spacetimes, to model quantum fields on cosmological backgrounds, especially when causal set de Sitter studies find new vacua and FLRW studies find super-horizon correlations without an inflation-like rapid expansion phase?

evidence.quote: Choosing a state in arbitrary curved spacetimes is a notorious challenge as there is no unique or obvious choice, and different choices lead to different consequences.

The Sorkin-Johnston (SJ) state is a choice of vacuum state in any arbitrary curved spacetime that is a candidate for circumventing this challenge. The SJ state is unique and distinguished in any globally hyperbolic spacetime and typically reflects the symmetries of the background spacetime (if there are any).

In the work in FLRW, correlations on super-horizon scales were found, without the help of a phase of rapid (inflation-like) expansion. It would be interesting to explore the phenomenological consequences of these findings regarding the SJ state.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime and let $\phi$ be a free real scalar quantum field on $M$. The Pauli–Jordan (commutator) function $i\Delta(x,y) = [\phi(x),\phi(y)]$ defines, via the spacetime volume measure, a self-adjoint operator $i\hat{\Delta}$ on $L^{2}(M)$. The Sorkin–Johnston (SJ) two-point function is defined as the positive part of $i\hat{\Delta}$, i.e.
$$W_{\mathrm{SJ}}(x,y) = \langle x | \mathrm{Pos}(i\hat{\Delta}) | y \rangle,$$
which uniquely determines a pure quasi-free ("vacuum") state $\omega_{\mathrm{SJ}}$ of the field whenever the spectral decomposition is well-defined. The same construction applies on a causal set $(C,\preceq)$, where $i\Delta$ becomes a finite antisymmetric matrix and $W_{\mathrm{SJ}}$ is again its positive spectral part.

Assume the background spacetime is a spatially flat Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker (FLRW) cosmology with metric
$$ds^{2} = -dt^{2} + a(t)^{2}\,d\mathbf{x}^{2},$$
without any phase of exponentially rapid (inflationary) expansion of $a(t)$. Suppose that the SJ two-point function $W_{\mathrm{SJ}}(x,y)$ for $\phi$ on such a background exhibits non-vanishing equal-time spatial correlations
$$\langle \phi(t,\mathbf{x})\,\phi(t,\mathbf{y}) \rangle_{\mathrm{SJ}}$$
at comoving separations $|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}|$ exceeding the comoving particle horizon at time $t$. Assume analogous studies of the SJ state on causal sets approximating de Sitter spacetime have produced vacuum states distinct from the standard Bunch–Davies/Euclidean vacuum.

Problem. Determine the observable cosmological consequences of adopting the Sorkin–Johnston state $\omega_{\mathrm{SJ}}$ as the vacuum state for quantum matter fields on cosmological backgrounds. In particular:

(i) Compute the predicted scalar (and, where appropriate, tensor) power spectrum
$$\mathcal{P}_{\phi}(k,t) := \frac{k^{3}}{2\pi^{2}}\,|\widetilde{W}_{\mathrm{SJ}}(k,t)|$$
arising from the SJ super-horizon correlations on an FLRW background without inflation, and compare its amplitude, tilt, and Gaussianity properties with the observed cosmic microwave background and large-scale-structure spectra.

(ii) Quantify the renormalized expectation value $\langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle_{\mathrm{SJ}}$ of the stress-energy tensor in the SJ state on FLRW and de Sitter backgrounds, and determine the resulting semiclassical backreaction on the scale factor $a(t)$.

(iii) Identify whether the new SJ vacua found on causal-set de Sitter approximations leave distinguishable imprints (e.g., modifications of the spectral tilt, running, non-Gaussianity, or discreteness-induced features at small scales) on cosmological observables that could be tested against CMB or large-scale-structure data.
artifact.status_search_result: The Sorkin–Johnston state has been studied in de Sitter, FLRW, and trousers spacetimes, and its coupling to gravity has been investigated (e.g., backreaction computations finding a large trace anomaly). However, a systematic derivation of observable cosmological consequences — including power spectra and backreaction on FLRW without inflation — based on SJ super-horizon correlations and the new causal-set de Sitter vacua has not been carried out. The question appears to remain open as a phenomenological program.

status_evidence.title: Coupling the Sorkin-Johnston State to Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Computes the renormalized stress-tensor of the SJ state and its backreaction; finds a large trace anomaly.
status_evidence.claim: SJ-gravity coupling has been studied but full cosmological observational consequences are not derived.

status_evidence.title: The Sorkin-Johnston State in a Patch of the Trousers Spacetime
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates SJ state in topology-changing spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: SJ state remains an active research topic in curved/causal-set backgrounds.
